node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Outcome value mapping
node.description: Map each outcome of a chance process to the numerical value assigned by a random variable.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Random variable support
node.description: Identify the set of possible values a discrete random variable can take.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Event from random variable value
node.description: Translate statements such as X equals 2 or X is at least 3 into events in the underlying sample space.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Distribution table representation
node.description: Represent a discrete random variable using a table pairing each possible value with its probability.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Probability mass function notation
node.description: Use notation such as P(X equals x) to describe probabilities assigned to values of a discrete random variable.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Nonnegative probability check
node.description: Check that every probability in a discrete distribution is zero or positive.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Probability sum check
node.description: Check that the probabilities across all possible values of a discrete random variable sum to one.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Missing probability value in distribution
node.description: Find a missing probability in a discrete distribution by using the requirement that all probabilities sum to one.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Cumulative probability for discrete random variables
node.description: Find probabilities such as P(X less than or equal to k) by summing the probabilities of relevant discrete values.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Build distribution from context
node.description: Construct a discrete probability distribution from a contextual chance process by identifying values and probabilities.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Discrete distribution bar chart
node.description: Represent a discrete probability distribution using a bar chart with values on one axis and probabilities on the other.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Expected value formula
node.description: Calculate expected value by summing each possible value multiplied by its probability.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Expected value long-run interpretation
node.description: Interpret expected value as a long-run average over many repetitions, not necessarily a value that occurs on one trial.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Expected gain or loss
node.description: Calculate and interpret expected gain or loss in games, decisions and financial contexts.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Fair game expected value
node.description: Use expected value to decide whether a simple game is fair, favourable or unfavourable.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Compare distributions by expected value
node.description: Compare discrete distributions using expected value as a measure of centre or long-run average outcome.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Variance of a discrete random variable introduction
node.description: Calculate and interpret variance as the expected squared distance from the mean for a discrete random variable.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Standard deviation of a discrete random variable introduction
node.description: Interpret standard deviation as the typical spread of values around the expected value for a discrete random variable.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Compare distributions by spread
node.description: Compare discrete distributions using variance or standard deviation as measures of spread.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Expected value reasonableness check
node.description: Check whether an expected value is reasonable by comparing it with the possible values and their probabilities.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Discrete distribution probabilities are valid
node.description: Every probability in a discrete distribution must be nonnegative and the full set of probabilities must sum to one.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Expected value is sum of x times probability
node.description: For a discrete random variable, expected value is found by summing each value multiplied by its probability.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Fair game has zero expected gain
node.description: A fair game in gain-loss terms has expected gain equal to zero for the player after costs and payoffs are included.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Standard deviation measures spread
node.description: For a distribution, standard deviation describes spread around the expected value in the original units of the random variable.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Random variable is just the random outcome
node.description: Learner treats a random variable as the physical random outcome itself rather than a numerical rule applied to outcomes.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Probabilities need not sum to one
node.description: Learner accepts a listed probability distribution even when the probabilities are negative or do not sum to one.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Expected value is most likely outcome
node.description: Learner interprets expected value as the most likely individual outcome rather than the long-run weighted average.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Fair game means equal chance to win
node.description: Learner judges monetary game fairness only by equal chance of winning, ignoring payoff sizes and costs.

edge.rationale: Mapping outcomes to values directly practises the meaning of a random variable.
Distribution tables are a central representation for discrete probability distributions.
Checking the probability sum directly practises distribution validity.
The expected value formula is central to introductory expected value work.
Variance is a common extension when working with discrete random variables and distributions.
Mapping outcomes to values requires knowing the underlying sample space.
edge.failure_signal: Learner assigns values without identifying the outcomes being mapped.

edge.rationale: The support is the set of values produced by the outcome-to-value mapping.
edge.failure_signal: Learner lists outcomes rather than possible random variable values.

edge.rationale: Events involving a random variable require knowing the values the variable can take.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot translate X greater than 2 into matching outcomes or values.

edge.rationale: A distribution table lists the support values and their probabilities.
edge.failure_signal: Learner omits possible values or includes impossible values in the distribution table.

edge.rationale: PMF notation formalises the same value-probability pairs shown in a distribution table.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats P(X=x) as a value of X rather than a probability assigned to a value.

edge.rationale: Distribution probabilities must each be valid probability values.
edge.failure_signal: Learner accepts a negative probability entry in a distribution.

edge.rationale: Checking a distribution is valid includes checking nonnegative entries and total probability one.
edge.failure_signal: Learner checks only the total and misses a negative probability entry.

edge.rationale: Finding a missing probability uses the sum-to-one requirement.
edge.failure_signal: Learner subtracts from 100 after using decimal probabilities or ignores one probability entry.

edge.rationale: Cumulative discrete probabilities are found by summing relevant entries in the distribution table.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses a single probability instead of summing all values in the range.

edge.rationale: Building a distribution from context requires translating value statements into underlying events.
edge.failure_signal: Learner assigns probabilities to values without counting the outcomes that generate them.

edge.rationale: A discrete distribution bar chart is drawn from value-probability pairs in a distribution table.
edge.failure_signal: Learner plots outcomes, counts or cumulative totals instead of probabilities by value.

edge.rationale: Expected value is calculated from the values and probabilities in the distribution.
edge.failure_signal: Learner averages the values without weighting by probability.

edge.rationale: Interpreting expected value follows from calculating it as a weighted average.
edge.failure_signal: Learner expects the exact expected value to occur on the next trial.

edge.rationale: Expected gain/loss applies expected value to payoff distributions.
edge.failure_signal: Learner ignores costs or payoff sizes when evaluating the long-run average gain.

edge.rationale: Fair-game evaluation uses expected gain or loss after costs and payoffs are included.
edge.failure_signal: Learner judges fairness by equal chance of winning rather than expected gain.

edge.rationale: Comparing expected values depends on interpreting expected value as centre or long-run average.
edge.failure_signal: Learner chooses a distribution based only on the maximum possible outcome.

edge.rationale: Variance is calculated from distances from the expected value.
edge.failure_signal: Learner computes spread without reference to the mean or expected value.

edge.rationale: Standard deviation is the square root of variance and returns spread to original units.
edge.failure_signal: Learner interprets variance and standard deviation interchangeably without units.

edge.rationale: Comparing spread relies on interpreting standard deviation or variance across distributions.
edge.failure_signal: Learner says distributions with equal expected value are identical despite different spreads.

edge.rationale: Reasonableness checks compare the calculated expected value with the possible values and probabilities.
edge.failure_signal: Learner accepts an expected value far outside the range of possible values without question.
